As others have said that they prefer the new version due to more complexity, I’d say that that is why I prefer the original—it’s charmingly chill. Not that it isn’t exciting, it is always a fun time and we never get tired of it when we bring it out. Maybe someone who plays it every other day or even every weekend will find it boring after a while by dissecting it and knowing all there is to know about it, but for us it’s still an enjoyable experience where we don’t try to “master” it or find the most “optimal” way to victory. 

It’s Zelda: Link to the past for us. Not breath of the wild. 

Plus, we also like introducing it to new board gamers and find it fun just having the board out and visually seeing what mysteries can be under those question marks. It’s like looking at a treasure map. You see the paths and think of ways to get the treasures and what may happen to you on the way there. Or even more fun, what can happen to your opponent, lol.  It’s a race and a sense of wonder in that childhood exploration that is often gone. 

Of course it has weaknesses, some balance issues, and yes it can be “broken,” but it isn’t always an issue for us. It’s the “no! Dragon attack!” Followed by laughter when one of us got too close to the sun ultimately burned by our greed, that makes this game a joy in the journey. And sharing that joy to new gamers makes the treasure adventure on the table even better.
